{"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-sonnet-5-5","id":"msg_011CgS1R5oqEh2iyRaXrGTkY","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"=== BEGIN ARTIFACT ARCHITECTURE.md ===\n# ARCHITECTURE: LayersTesting\n\n| Field       | Value |\n|-------------|-------|\n| Version     | 20261027 V1 |\n| Description | Modules, boundaries, and technical decisions for the LayersTesting command-line cash ledger. |\n| Provides    | python-foundation |\n\n## Questions\n\n- None.\n\n## Purpose\n\nLayersTesting is a command-line cash ledger. The executable `ledger` at the application root keeps accounts, categories, and cash transactions in SQLite. Every command validates all inputs and rules before its first write, then writes all of its changes or none. Reports are computed from stored rows at the time of the command.\n\n## Technology Stack\n\nDerived from `TECHNOLOGY_STACK.md`, which remains the decision of record.\n\n| Technology | Where it applies |\n|---|---|\n| Python 3.11+ | Implementation language for every module. |\n| SQLite | The database, reached only through the shipped `persistence` package. |\n| CLI | The `ledger` executable and the `cli` package. |\n| pytest | Test runner behind `bin/test.sh` and the `tests/` suite. |\n| POSIX sh | `bin/test.sh`, the `ledger` launcher, and the supplied grader. |\n\n## Project Layout\n\n| Path | Role |\n|---|---|\n| `ledger` | Executable launcher at the application root; uses the `.venv` interpreter when present, else `python3`; calls `cli.main` and exits with its return value. |\n| `pyproject.toml`, `uv.lock` | Dependency manifest and committed lock. The environment is `.venv` created by `uv venv`. |\n| `conftest.py` | Exposes the `db_session` and `cli_runner` fixtures. |\n| `bin/` | Launchers, including `bin/test.sh`. |\n| `persistence/` | Generated by Drydock from `DATABASE.md`; never written by hand. |\n| `ledgerapp/` | Shared application modules: `config.py`, `errors.py`, `money.py`, and later `validators.py`. |\n| `cli/` | Entry point `main`, `registry.py`, `output.py`, `testing.py`, and `commands/`. |\n| `cli/commands/` | One module per command group. Every module in the package is imported automatically, so a story adds a command by adding a module. |\n| `tests/` | The application's own pytest suite. |\n\n## Module Ownership\n\n| Boundary | Owning module | May access |\n|---|---|---|\n| Persistence | `persistence` (generated) | The SQLite driver. Nothing else imports a driver. |\n| Configuration | `ledgerapp/config.py` | Environment variables `DATABASE_URL`, `DATABASE_PATH`; opens the store through `persistence.open_database`. |\n| Money | `ledgerapp/money.py` | Parses and formats integer cents. No floating point at any layer. |\n| Errors and exit codes | `ledgerapp/errors.py` | Defines the error classes and their exit codes. |\n| Command dispatch and output | `cli/` | Calls handlers; owns stdout and stderr writing. |\n| Command handlers | `cli/commands/*` | `db.<table>.<operation>(...)` only. No SQL, table names, or driver imports. |\n\n## Technical Decisions\n\n- Handlers are plain functions `handler(args, db)` that validate every input and rule before their first write and return a list of CSV rows (each a list of strings) or `None`.\n- Multi-row writes (load, transfer, init) validate completely first, then write inside one transaction of the shipped persistence library, so a failure leaves no partial rows.\n- Amounts are integer cents everywhere; output formatting is done with integer arithmetic.\n- Application code never reads `sources/run.sh` or any seed file; seed files reach the database only through `ledger load`.\n- No DDL runs at runtime. The schema is applied at the DATABASE step; `init` empties tables through the `delete_all` operations.\n- Diagnostics go to standard error and are never compared.\n\n## Exit Codes\n\n| Code | Meaning |\n|---|---|\n| 0 | Success |\n| 1 | Operational failure: the database cannot be opened or a named file cannot be read |\n| 2 | Usage error |\n| 3 | Rejected |\n| 4 | Not found |\n\n## Programmatic Acceptance\n\n=== AC foundation-python-manifest ===\nIntent: The project declares Python 3.11 or newer in a parseable pyproject.toml, the running interpreter satisfies it, and a committed uv.lock exists.\n\nimport pathlib\nimport sys\nimport tomllib\n\nassert sys.version_info >= (3, 11)\npyproject = pathlib.Path(\"pyproject.toml\")\nassert pyproject.is_file(), \"foundation not built: pyproject.toml missing\"\ndata = tomllib.loads(pyproject.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\"))\nassert \"project\" in data\nassert \"requires-python\" in data[\"project\"]\nassert pathlib.Path(\"uv.lock\").is_file()\n=== END AC foundation-python-manifest ===\n\n=== AC foundation-launcher-dir ===\nIntent: The bin directory exists for launchers and the shared application package imports.\n\nimport importlib\nimport pathlib\n\nassert pathlib.Path(\"bin\").is_dir(), \"foundation not built: bin/ missing\"\nmodule = importlib.import_module(\"ledgerapp\")\nassert module is not None\n=== END AC foundation-launcher-dir ===\n\n=== AC foundation-conftest-fixtures ===\nIntent: conftest.py defines the db_session and cli_runner fixtures that the project's pytest suite receives.\n\nimport ast\nimport pathlib\n\nconftest = pathlib.Path(\"conftest.py\")\nassert conftest.is_file(), \"foundation not built: conftest.py missing\"\ntree = ast.parse(conftest.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\"))\ndefined = {node.name for node in ast.walk(tree) if isinstance(node, ast.FunctionDef)}\nrequired = {\"db_session\", \"cli_runner\"}\nassert required <= defined\n=== END AC foundation-conftest-fixtures ===\n\n## User Acceptance\n\n- None.\n\n## Guardrails\n\n- Do not read `sources/run.sh` or any seed file from application code.\n- Do not open a database driver outside the shipped persistence library.\n- Do not use floating point for money at any layer.\n- Do not modify any file under `sources/`.\n=== END ARTIFACT ===\n=== BEGIN ARTIFACT FEATURE-DatabaseSelection.md ===\n# FEATURE: Database Selection\n\n| Field       | Value |\n|-------------|-------|\n| Version     | 20261027 V1 |\n| Description | Resolve the database location from configuration and open the store through the shipped persistence library. |\n| Depends On  | ARCHITECTURE.md, DATABASE.md |\n| Provides    | config.database_path, config.open_store |\n\n## Questions\n\n- None.\n\n## Purpose\n\nEvery command reads its database location from one place. `ledgerapp/config.py` resolves it and opens the store.\n\n## Behavior\n\n- `database_path() -> str` reads the environment at each call. It returns `DATABASE_URL` when set and non-empty, with one leading `sqlite://` prefix removed if present. Otherwise it returns `DATABASE_PATH` when set and non-empty. Otherwise it returns `data/app.db`.\n- `open_store()` opens the resolved path through `persistence.open_database` and returns the `Database`. For the default path only, it first creates the parent directory if absent. For any other path no directory is created.\n- When the database cannot be opened, `open_store()` raises `ledgerapp.errors.StoreUnavailable` (exit code 1). The CLI maps it to exit 1 with nothing on standard output and no record changed.\n- This module imports no database driver and applies no DDL.\n\n## Database Interface\n\n- None — persistence is owned ===\n\n## User Acceptance\n\n- None.\n\n## Guardrails\n\n- Do not import a database driver in this module.\n- Do not apply DDL or create tables when opening the store.\n- Create a directory only for the default path `data/app.db`.\n=== END ARTIFACT ===\n=== BEGIN ARTIFACT FEATURE-LedgerCli.md ===\n# FEATURE: Ledger CLI Foundation\n\n| Field       | Value |\n|-------------|-------|\n| Version     | 20261027 V1 |\n| Description | The ledger executable, the cli package entry point, command dispatch, CSV output, money handling, and exit-code mapping. |\n| Depends On  | ARCHITECTURE.md, FEATURE-DatabaseSelection.md |\n| Provides    | ledger, cli.main |\n| Consumes    | config.open_store |\n\n## Questions\n\n- None.\n\n## Purpose\n\nProvide the shared command machinery every later command story registers into.\n\n## Interface\n\n- `ledger` at the application root: a POSIX sh launcher that runs `cli.main` with the `.venv` interpreter when present, else `python3`, and exits with the returned code.\n- `cli.main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int`. `None` means `sys.argv[1:]`.\n- `cli.testing.cli_runner(*args) -> (exit_code, stdout, stderr)` per the CLI Foundation Contract. `main` resolves `sys.stdout` and `sys.stderr` at call time so redirection works.\n- `cli.registry.register(path: tuple[str, ...], handler, needs_store: bool = True)`; a handler is `handler(args: list[str], db) -> list[list[str]] | None`. Modules in `cli/commands/` are imported automatically, so adding a module registers its commands.\n- `cli.output`: renders rows as CSV: comma-separated, no quoting, `\\n` line endings.\n- `ledgerapp.errors`: `LedgerError` with an `exit_code`; `StoreUnavailable` (1), `FileUnreadable` (1), `UsageError` (2), `Rejected` (3), `NotFound` (4).\n- `ledgerapp.money`: `parse_amount(text) -> int` converts `-?DIGITS[.D[D]]` with at most two decimals, never zero, to integer cents using integer arithmetic and raises `Rejected` otherwise; `format_cents(cents: int) -> str` writes exactly two decimals, a leading `-` when negative, and no thousands separator.\n\n## Dispatch\n\n1. Resolve the command by the longest registered prefix of the arguments. No arguments, an unknown command, or a known group with a missing or unknown subcommand raises `UsageError` before the store is opened.\n2. When `needs_store`, open the store with `config.open_store()`; failure exits 1.\n3. Call the handler with the remaining arguments. Output is written only after the handler returns, so a failing command writes nothing to standard output.\n4. A `LedgerError` writes one diagnostic line naming the problem to standard error and returns its exit code. Any other exception writes one line to standard error and returns 1.\n\n## Database Interface\n\n- None — persistence is owned by DATABASE.md.\n\n## Programmatic Acceptance\n\n=== AC cli-main-returns-int ===\nIntent: cli.main is callable with an argument list and returns an integer exit code; an unknown command is a usage error with empty standard output.\n\nimport cli\nfrom cli.testing import cli_runner\n\nassert callable(cli.main)\ncode, out, err = cli_runner(\"zzfrobnicate\")\nprint(out)\nprint(err)\nassert isinstance(code, int)\nassert code == 2\nassert out == \"\"\n=== END AC cli-main-returns-int ===\n\n=== AC cli-no-arguments-usage ===\nIntent: Calling the CLI with no arguments is a usage error that writes one diagnostic line to standard error and nothing to standard output.\n\nfrom cli.testing import cli_runner\n\ncode, out, err = cli_runner()\nprint(out)\nprint(err)\nassert code == 2\nassert out == \"\"\nassert len(err.splitlines()) == 1\n=== END AC cli-no-arguments-usage ===\n\n=== AC cli-exit-code-mapping ===\nIntent: Success returns 0 and writes the rows as CSV; each error class maps to its exit code with empty standard output and one diagnostic line.\n\nfrom cli import registry\nfrom cli.testing import cli_runner\nfrom ledgerapp import errors\n\nrows = [[\"alpha\", \"beta\"], [\"gamma\", \"delta\"]]\nexpected_out = \"\".join(\",\".join(row) + \"\\n\" for row in rows)\n\n\ndef ok(args, db):\n    return rows\n\n\ndef make_raiser(exc_type):\n    def handler(args, db):\n        raise exc_type(\"probe diagnostic\")\n    return handler\n\n\nregistry.register((\"zzprobe\", \"ok\"), ok, needs_store=False)\ncases = [\n    (\"rejected\", errors.Rejected, 3),\n    (\"notfound\", errors.NotFound, 4),\n    (\"usage\", errors.UsageError, 2),\n    (\"unreadable\", errors.FileUnreadable, 1),\n    (\"unavailable\", errors.StoreUnavailable, 1),\n]\nfor name, exc_type, want_code in cases:\n    registry.register((\"zzprobe\", name), make_raiser(exc_type), needs_store=False)\n\ncode, out, err = cli_runner(\"zzprobe\", \"ok\")\nprint(out)\nprint(err)\nassert code == 0\nassert out == expected_out\n\nfor name, exc_type, want_code in cases:\n    code, out, err = cli_runner(\"zzprobe\", name)\n    print(name, code, out, err)\n    assert code == want_code\n    assert out == \"\"\n BEGIN ARTIFACT ARCHITECTURE.md ===\n# ARCHITECTURE: LayersTesting\n\n| Field       | Value |\n|-------------|-------|\n| Version     | 20261027 V1 |\n| Description | Modules, boundaries, and technical decisions for the LayersTesting command-line cash ledger. |\n| Provides    | python-foundation |\n\n## Questions\n\n- None.\n\n## Purpose\n\nLayersTesting is a command-line cash ledger. The executable `ledger` at the application root keeps accounts, categories, and cash transactions in SQLite. Every command validates all inputs and rules before its first write, then writes all of its changes or none. Reports are computed from stored rows at the time of the command.\n\n## Technology Stack\n\nDerived from `TECHNOLOGY_STACK.md`, which remains the decision of record.\n\n| Technology | Where it applies |\n|---|---|\n| Python 3.11+ | Implementation language for every module. |\n| SQLite | The database, reached only through the shipped `persistence` package. |\n| CLI | The `ledger` executable and the `cli` package. |\n| pytest | Test runner behind `bin/test.sh` and the `tests/` suite. |\n| POSIX sh | `bin/test.sh`, the `ledger` launcher, and the supplied grader. |\n\n## Project Layout\n\n| Path | Role |\n|---|---|\n| `ledger` | Executable launcher at the application root; uses the `.venv` interpreter when present, else `python3`; calls `cli.main` and exits with its return value. |\n| `pyproject.toml`, `uv.lock` | Dependency manifest and committed lock. The environment is `.venv` created by `uv venv`. |\n| `conftest.py` | Exposes the `db_session` and `cli_runner` fixtures. |\n| `bin/` | Launchers, including `bin/test.sh`. |\n| `persistence/` | Generated by Drydock from `DATABASE.md`; never written by hand. |\n| `ledgerapp/` | Shared application modules: `config.py`, `errors.py`, `money.py`, and later `validators.py`. |\n| `cli/` | Entry point `main`, `registry.py`, `output.py`, `testing.py`, and `commands/`. |\n| `cli/commands/` | One module per command group. Every module in the package is imported automatically, so a story adds a command by adding a module. |\n| `tests/` | The application's own pytest suite. |\n\n## Module Ownership\n\n| Boundary | Owning module | May access |\n|---|---|---|\n| Persistence | `persistence` (generated) | The SQLite driver. Nothing else imports a driver. |\n| Configuration | `ledgerapp/config.py` | Environment variables `DATABASE_URL`, `DATABASE_PATH`; opens the store through `persistence.open_database`. |\n| Money | `ledgerapp/money.py` | Parses and formats integer cents. No floating point at any layer. |\n| Errors and exit codes | `ledgerapp/errors.py` | Defines the error classes and their exit codes. |\n| Command dispatch and output | `cli/` | Calls handlers; owns stdout and stderr writing. |\n| Command handlers | `cli/commands/*` | `db.<table>.<operation>(...)` only. No SQL, table names, or driver imports. |\n\n## Technical Decisions\n\n- Handlers are plain functions `handler(args, db)` that validate every input and rule before their first write and return a list of CSV rows (each a list of strings) or `None`.\n- Multi-row writes (load, transfer, init) validate completely first, then write inside one transaction of the shipped persistence library, so a failure leaves no partial rows.\n- Amounts are integer cents everywhere; output formatting is done with integer arithmetic.\n- Application code never reads `sources/run.sh` or any seed file; seed files reach the database only through `ledger load`.\n- No DDL runs at runtime. The schema is applied at the DATABASE step; `init` empties tables through the `delete_all` operations.\n- Diagnostics go to standard error and are never compared.\n\n## Exit Codes\n\n| Code | Meaning |\n|---|---|\n| 0 | Success |\n| 1 | Operational failure: the database cannot be opened or a named file cannot be read |\n| 2 | Usage error |\n| 3 | Rejected |\n| 4 | Not found |\n\n## Programmatic Acceptance\n\n=== AC foundation-python-manifest ===\nIntent: The project declares Python 3.11 or newer in a parseable pyproject.toml, the running interpreter satisfies it, and a committed uv.lock exists.\n\nimport pathlib\nimport sys\nimport tomllib\n\nassert sys.version_info >= (3, 11)\npyproject = pathlib.Path(\"pyproject.toml\")\nassert pyproject.is_file(), \"foundation not built: pyproject.toml missing\"\ndata = tomllib.loads(pyproject.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\"))\nassert \"project\" in data\nassert \"requires-python\" in data[\"project\"]\nassert pathlib.Path(\"uv.lock\").is_file()\n=== END AC foundation-python-manifest ===\n\n=== AC foundation-launcher-dir ===\nIntent: The bin directory exists for launchers and the shared application package imports.\n\nimport importlib\nimport pathlib\n\nassert pathlib.Path(\"bin\").is_dir(), \"foundation not built: bin/ missing\"\nmodule = importlib.import_module(\"ledgerapp\")\nassert module is not None\n=== END AC foundation-launcher-dir ===\n\n=== AC foundation-conftest-fixtures ===\nIntent: conftest.py defines the db_session and cli_runner fixtures that the project's pytest suite receives.\n\nimport ast\nimport pathlib\n\nconftest = pathlib.Path(\"conftest.py\")\nassert conftest.is_file(), \"foundation not built: conftest.py missing\"\ntree = ast.parse(conftest.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\"))\ndefined = {node.name for node in ast.walk(tree) if isinstance(node, ast.FunctionDef)}\nrequired = {\"db_session\", \"cli_runner\"}\nassert required <= defined\n=== END AC foundation-conftest-fixtures ===\n\n## User Acceptance\n\n- None.\n\n## Guardrails\n\n- Do not read `sources/run.sh` or any seed file from application code.\n- Do not open a database driver outside the shipped persistence library.\n- Do not use floating point for money at any layer.\n- Do not modify any file under `sources/`.\n=== END ARTIFACT ===\n=== BEGIN ARTIFACT FEATURE-DatabaseSelection.md ===\n# FEATURE: Database Selection\n\n| Field       | Value |\n|-------------|-------|\n| Version     | 20261027 V1 |\n| Description | Resolve the database location from configuration and open the store through the shipped persistence library. |\n| Depends On  | ARCHITECTURE.md, DATABASE.md |\n| Provides    | config.database_path, config.open_store |\n\n## Questions\n\n- None.\n\n## Purpose\n\nEvery command reads its database location from one place. `ledgerapp/config.py` resolves it and opens the store.\n\n## Behavior\n\n- `database_path() -> str` reads the environment at each call. It returns `DATABASE_URL` when set and non-empty, with one leading `sqlite://` prefix removed if present. Otherwise it returns `DATABASE_PATH` when set and non-empty. Otherwise it returns `data/app.db`.\n- `open_store()` opens the resolved path through `persistence.open_database` and returns the `Database`. For the default path only, it first creates the parent directory if absent. the default path `data/app.db`.\n=== END ARTIFACT ===\n=== BEGIN ARTIFACT FEATURE-LedgerCli.md ===\n# FEATURE: Ledger CLI Foundation\n\n| Field       | Value |\n|-------------|-------|\n| Version     | 20261027 V1 |\n| Description | The ledger executable, the cli package entry point, command dispatch, CSV output, money handling, and exit-code mapping. |\n| Depends On  | ARCHITECTURE.md, FEATURE-DatabaseSelection.md |\n| Provides    | ledger, cli.main |\n| Consumes    | config.open_store |\n\n## Questions\n\n- None.\n\n## Purpose\n\nProvide the shared command machinery every later command story registers into.\n\n## Interface\n\n- `ledger` at the application root: a POSIX sh launcher that runs `cli.main` with the `.venv` interpreter when present, else `python3`, and exits with the returned code.\n- `cli.main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int`. `None` means `sys.argv[1:]`.\n- `cli.testing.cli_runner(*args) -> (exit_code, stdout, stderr)` per the CLI Foundation Contract. `main` resolves `sys.stdout` and `sys.stderr` at call time so redirection works.\n- `cli.registry.register(path: tuple[str, ...], handler, needs_store: bool = True)`; a handler is `handler(args: list[str], db) -> list[list[str]] | None`. Modules in `cli/commands/` are imported automatically, so adding a module registers its commands.\n- `cli.output`: renders rows as CSV: comma-separated, no quoting, `\\n` line endings.\n- `ledgerapp.errors`: `LedgerError` with an `exit_code`; `StoreUnavailable` (1), `FileUnreadable` (1), `UsageError` (2), `Rejected` (3), `NotFound` (4).\n- `ledgerapp.money`: `parse_amount(text) -> int` converts `-?DIGITS[.D[D]]` with at most two decimals, never zero, to integer cents using integer arithmetic and raises `Rejected` otherwise; `format_cents(cents: int) -> str` writes exactly two decimals, a leading `-` when negative, and no thousands separator.\n\n## Dispatch\n\n1. Resolve the command by the longest registered prefix of the arguments. No arguments, an unknown command, or a known group with a missing or unknown subcommand raises `UsageError` before the store is opened.\n2. When `needs_store`, open the store with `config.open_store()`; failure exits 1.\n3. Call the handler with the remaining arguments. Output is written only after the handler returns, so a failing command writes nothing to standard output.\n4. A `LedgerError` writes one diagnostic line naming the problem to standard error and returns its exit code. Any other exception writes one line to standard error and returns 1.\n\n## Database Interface\n\n- None — persistence is owned by DATABASE.md.\n\n## Programmatic Acceptance\n\n=== AC cli-main-returns-int ===\nIntent: cli.main is callable with an argument list and returns an integer exit code; an unknown command is a usage error with empty standard output.\n\nimport cli\nfrom cli.testing import cli_runner\n\nassert callable(cli.main)\ncode, out, err = cli_runner(\"zzfrobnicate\")\nprint(out)\nprint(err)\nassert isinstance(code, int)\nassert code == 2\nassert out == \"\"\n=== END AC cli-main-returns-int ===\n\n=== AC cli-no-arguments-usage ===\nIntent: Calling the CLI with no arguments is a usage error that writes one diagnostic line to standard error and nothing to standard output.\n\nfrom cli.testing import cli_runner\n\ncode, out, err = cli_runner()\nprint(out)\nprint(err)\nassert code == 2\nassert out == \"\"\nassert len(err.splitlines()) == 1\n=== END AC cli-no-arguments-usage ===\n\n=== AC cli-exit-code-mapping ===\nIntent: Success returns 0 and writes the rows as CSV; each error class maps to its exit code with empty standard output and one diagnostic line.\n\nfrom cli import registry\nfrom cli.testing import cli_runner\nfrom ledgerapp import errors\n\nrows = [[\"alpha\", \"beta\"], [\"gamma\", \"delta\"]]\nexpected_out = \"\".join(\",\".join(row) + \"\\n\" for row in rows)\n\n\ndef ok(args, db):\n    return rows\n\n\ndef make_raiser(exc_type):\n    def handler(args, db):\n        raise exc_type(\"probe diagnostic\")\n    return handler\n\n\nregistry.register((\"zzprobe\", \"ok\"), ok, needs_store=False)\ncases = [\n    (\"rejected\", errors.Rejected, 3),\n    (\"notfound\", errors.NotFound, 4),\n    (\"usage\", errors.UsageError, 2),\n    (\"unreadable\", errors.FileUnreadable, 1),\n    (\"unavailable\", errors.StoreUnavailable, 1),\n]\nfor name, exc_type, want_code in cases:\n    registry.register((\"zzprobe\", name), make_raiser(exc_type), needs_store=False)\n\ncode, out, err = cli_runner(\"zzprobe\", \"ok\")\nprint(out)\nprint(err)\nassert code == 0\nassert out == expected_out\n\nfor name, exc_type, want_code in cases:\n    code, out, err = cli_runner(\"zzprobe\", name)\n    print(name, code, out, err)\n    assert code == want_code\n    assert out == \"\"\n    assert len(err.splitlines()) == 1\n=== END AC cli-exit-code-mapping ===\n\n=== AC cli-group-needs-subcommand ===\nIntent: A known command group with a missing or unknown subcommand is a usage error, and a handler is not run.\n\nfrom cli import registry\nfrom cli.testing import cli_runner\n\ncalls = []\n\n\ndef handler(args, db):\n    calls.append(list(args))\n    return [[\"x\"]]\n\n\nregistry.register((\"zzgroup\", \"run\"), handler, needs_store=False)\n\ncode, out, err = cli_runner(\"zzgroup\")\nassert code == 2\nassert out == \"\"\ncode, out, err = cli_runner(\"zzgroup\", \"zzmissing\")\nassert code == 2\nassert out == \"\"\nassert calls == []\ncode, out, err = cli_runner(\"zzgroup\", \"run\", \"arg1\")\nassert code == 0\nassert calls == [[\"arg1\"]]\n=== END AC cli-group-needs-subcommand ===\n\n=== AC cli-executable-launcher ===\nIntent: The ledger launcher at the application root is executable and exits 2 with empty standard output for an unknown command.\n\nimport os\nimport subprocess\n\nassert os.path.isfile(\"ledger\"), \"foundation not built: ledger missing\"\nassert os.access(\"ledger\", os.X_OK)\nresult = subprocess.run([\"./ledger\", \"zzfrobnicate\"], capture_output=True, text=True)\nprint(result.stdout)\nprint(result.stderr)\nassert result.returncode == 2\nassert result.stdout == \"\"\n=== END AC cli-executable-launcher ===\n\n=== AC cli-money-format ===\nIntent: format_cents writes exactly two decimals, a leading minus for negatives, and no thousands separator; expectations are derived from assert money.format_cents(cents) == f\"{expected:.2f}\"\n=== END AC cli-money-format ===\n\n=== AC cli-money-parse-valid ===\nIntent: parse_amount converts valid decimal text to integer cents; expected cents are derived from the input text with Decimal.\n\nfrom decimal import Decimal\n\nfrom ledgerapp import money\n\nfor text in [\"45.50\", \"-12.5\", \"7\", \"-0.01\", \"5000.00\", \"0.1\"]:\n    expected = int(Decimal(text) * 100)\n    result = money.parse_amount(text)\n    assert isinstance(result, int)\n    assert result == expected\n=== END AC cli-money-parse-valid Purpose\n\n`ledger init` prepares an empty ledger for loading and use and removes existing ledger records when rerun.\n\n## Behavior\n\n- Takes no arguments; any argument is a usage error (exit 2).\n- Removes every transaction first, then every category and every account, in one persistence-library transaction, so foreign keys hold and the unit is atomic.\n- Writes nothing to standard output and exits 0. amount=1000, memo=\"\"\n    )\n    assert db.transactions.get(txn_id=920001) is not None\n    code, out, err = cli_runner(\"init\")\n    print(out)\n    print(err)\n    assert code == 0\n    assert
